title: SRE weekly ops sync + reliability review — prep and notes (2026-04-01)
content:
Goal: prep for weekly SRE ops sync + reliability review (aim: 30-40m). Quick summary of top issues, SLO posture, paging trends, and proposed agenda + action items.

Agenda (30-40m):
- 0-5m: Quick wins / shoutouts / housekeeping
- 5-15m: SLO status review (latency + availability for hosted API + Dedicated pools)
- 15-30m: Top incidents & postmortem highlights (2 deep dives)
- 30-35m: Paging trends and on-call load / rota adjustments
- 35-40m: Actions and owners + next steps

SLO snapshot (last 7 days / compare to 30d):
- Hosted API availability (global): 99.94% (7d drop: 0.08% vs 30d avg) - minor regional blip in us-west-2 2026-03-29 03:10-03:40 UTC (routing misconfig)
- Serving-runtime p99 latency (text generation end-to-end): 420ms (7d increase: +55ms) - correlated with increased small-burst tail from batch sizing change on 3/27
- Embeddings endpoint p95 latency: 310ms (within SLO)
- Dedicated pools throughput SLOs: met; one customer reported 2x slower cold-start on certain model variants (see JIRA-INC-4821)

Notes / context:
- Observability: trace sampling bump last week (temporary) might have affected profiler costs but helped find the KV-cache eviction pattern (see trace #TR-20260328-1).
- Autoscaler: config tweak on 3/27 to be more aggressive on pod consolidation - likely increased transient queuing for short bursts. Need to evaluate using synthetic load tests.

Top incidents (for this review) - pick 2:
1) INC-4821: Dedicated pool slow cold-starts for quantized-ggml-13b (customer-reported) - Severity: P2
   - Timeline: 2026-03-29 01:20 UTC - customer observed ~12s cold-starts on dedicated nodes; normal <5s.
   - Root cause hypothesis: delayed model warming due to lazy KV cache hydration + new q-kt loader race condition introduced in PR #987.
   - Impact: 1 external customer impacted (enterprise-dataplane), internal alerts triggered but suppressed by retention rule causing delayed pager escalation.
   - Mitigation: manual warmup script deployed to the pool (patch: add prefetch on model pull).
   - Next: PR to add deterministic prefetch + add unit test for q-kt loader race (owner: Alex Martin, target: 2026-04-08). Add canary to Dedicated rollout.
   - Linked: JIRA-INC-4821, PR #987, runbook: dedicated-coldstart-warmup (draft)

2) INC-4834: us-west-2 routing flap (hosted API partial outage) - Severity: P1 (brief)
   - Timeline: 2026-03-29 03:10-03:40 UTC - region showed increased 5xx rate and elevated fanout latencies.
   - Root cause: misapplied traffic-shift policy during an RBAC config change; automated fallback failed due to missing compatibility rule for legacy model alias.
   - Impact: ~2.5% of global traffic experienced errors (brief) - some customers auto-retried; some experienced degraded UX.
   - Mitigation: rolled back policy, emergency fix to add compatibility rule, re-enabled fallback routing.
   - Action: add policy validation step to CI + expand integration test matrix for legacy aliases (owner: Samira Patel, target: 2026-04-06).

Paging trends / on-call load:
- Weekly page count (last 4w): 18, 22, 34, 42 (uptrend).
- Top noise sources: noisy infra alerts during autoscaler tuning windows, transient 5xx spikes from regional rollouts, and flaky integration tests marking runbooks 'incident' prematurely.
- On-call fatigue signal: average time-on-call increased by ~30% (more mid-shift escalations). Need to consider a temporary bump in rotation capacity for next 2 weeks.

Proposed mitigations / priorities (short list):
- Immediate (this week):
  - Stabilize Dedicated cold-start mitigation: create canary + improve warmup (Alex).
  - CI policy validation for routing changes (Samira).
  - Adjust alert thresholds for autoscaler tuning jobs to reduce noise (Ethan).
- Medium (2-6 weeks):
  - Synthetic load tests for typical burst patterns; tune batching thresholds accordingly (owner: eng-serving-runtime team).
  - Improve runbook clarity so that integration-test-driven alerts don't trigger full pager (owner: eng-sre-runbooks).
  - Add SLO regression alerting tied to eval sets (proposed by product-optimize).

Open questions / stuff to discuss in the meeting:
- Risk tolerance: how aggressive do we want autoscaler consolidation to be during business hours? (ops vs cost).
- On-call support: approve temporary +1 headcount for rotations for next 2 weeks?
- Rollout cadence: require canary percentage floor before policy changes that affect routing.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Alex Martin: PR to add deterministic prefetch + q-kt loader test (target 2026-04-08) [JIRA-INC-4821].
- Samira Patel: Add routing policy CI validation + integration tests for legacy aliases (target 2026-04-06).
- Ethan Chen: Tune autoscaler alerting thresholds; propose new thresholds and post to #sre-alerts (target 2026-04-05).
- Jordan Lee (me): Draft temporary on-call rota bump proposal + cost estimate; sync with SRE manager (target 2026-04-03).
- Eng-sre-runbooks (assigned): Review runbooks that currently escalate based on integration-test failures; propose changes (target 2026-04-10).

Notes-to-self / meeting prep reminders:
- Bring short timeline slides for both incidents (1 slide each) + a quick metric chart (p99 latency trend last 30d).
- Have the runbook change examples ready to show (suppress vs suppress+info).
- If asked about capacity/cost tradeoffs: prepare numbers for cost delta of autoscaler consolidation at 10%/25%/50% (ask infra-finance for latest rate card).

Misc (scratchpad):
- Potential follow-up: schedule a joint postmortem with Dedicated infra + product owner for INC-4821 to capture customer impact and SLA credit discussion.
- Consider adding lightweight client-side warmup API for Dedicated customers to opt into (longer-term).

Meeting logistics:
- Time: Thu 2026-04-02 09:00 PT (confirm calendar invite)
- Attendees: eng-sre, serving-runtime leads, dedicated infra, product-optimize (optional), on-call rotation representatives

End of notes.

-- Jordan
